overview: The same species behaves like a completely different organism depending on whether it is floating free or embedded in a community.
genZNote: Alone it’s easy prey. Together it’s a fortress.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Free-floating, individual bacterial cells suspended in liquid.
aspects.valueB: Bacterial cells attached to a surface and enclosed within a self-produced extracellular matrix, living as a structured community.

aspects.label: Antibiotic Susceptibility
aspects.valueA: Generally susceptible at concentrations predicted by standard MIC testing.
aspects.valueB: Markedly more tolerant — can survive antibiotic concentrations many-fold higher than the planktonic MIC of the same strain.

aspects.label: Growth Rate
aspects.valueA: Typically faster, more uniform growth throughout the population.
aspects.valueB: Heterogeneous — includes slow-growing or dormant 'persister' subpopulations within the matrix.

aspects.label: Gene Expression Pattern
aspects.valueA: Reflects free-living metabolic and stress-response programs.
aspects.valueB: Distinct gene expression program, often coordinated via quorum sensing between cells.

aspects.label: Interaction With Host Immune System
aspects.valueA: More readily recognized and cleared by phagocytes and antibodies.
aspects.valueB: Matrix physically shields cells from phagocytosis and limits antibody/complement penetration.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Represents most standard clinical culture and susceptibility testing scenarios.
aspects.valueB: Underlies chronic and device-associated infections (catheters, prosthetic joints, cystic fibrosis lungs) that resist standard treatment.

aspects.label: Relevance to Standard Lab Testing
aspects.valueA: Standard MIC/susceptibility testing directly reflects this state.
aspects.valueB: Standard MIC testing systematically underestimates the antibiotic dose actually needed to treat biofilm-associated infection.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Free-floating and drug-susceptible at predicted MICs.
aspects.valueB: Matrix-embedded and dramatically more antibiotic-tolerant than the same strain in planktonic form.

overlay.commonMisconception: A biofilm organism isn't genetically more resistant — its MIC on a lab plate can look identical; the tolerance comes from the matrix and physiology, not new resistance genes.
